sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- CENTCOM's own announcement, Nov 7] CENTCOM Commander Adm. Brad Cooper directed the creation of Task Force Iron Gate on Nov 7: a ~20-person civilian+military staff based in Tampa, Florida, coordinating with other US government agencies to 'monitor, detect, and disrupt' movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and illegal revenue streams across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. CENTCOM says the unit reinforces the naval blockade, which it estimates has halted Iranian crude exports worth more than $25 billion. CENTCOM's graphic names Iran's borders with Turkiye, Afghanistan, Turkmenistan and Pakistan as focus areas. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- Reuters/JPost] The announcement had not been previously reported; Reuters saw the statement ahead of its release. Cooper: 'Strengthening Centcom's collaboration with US interagency partners will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military.' [SCOPE NOTE] The statement gives no details on where the task force will operate, what authorities it will use, or how it will interact with neighbouring states; it is a coordination/planning cell, not a deployed force. [DATE CONFLICT -- DO NOT MERGE] Khaleej Times says the naval blockade was imposed April 13, 2026; Turkiye Today dates the port-covering naval blockade to July 2026. Both are carried as stated; the discrepancy is unresolved.
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct publisher families with declared tiers: CENTCOM/US DoD (T1, STATE US -- the primary source itself), Reuters (T1 wire), Jerusalem Post (T3). Arab News, Dawn, Khaleej Times, Kurdistan24, Turkiye Today, Times Now, Geopolitiki carry the CENTCOM statement / Reuters wire and do not add families.
sections.what_disputed: No counter-statement from Iran on Iron Gate yet in-window. CSIS June 2026 assessment (cited by Times Now) had already identified the Caspian as a potential Iran procurement corridor -- the task force follows a known analysis, not a new intelligence claim. The $25B crude-halt figure is CENTCOM's own estimate, not independently audited. Naval-blockade start date conflicts between carriers (April 13 vs July 2026) -- see claim.
sections.why_matters: The blockade just went inland -- CENTCOM's new Iron Gate task force targets Iran's land and Caspian lifelines after $25 billion of oil was stopped at sea.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (CENTCOM statement first surfaced ~17:20 via Reuters/Arab News; the 1800-04 triage wrongly recorded 'no CENTCOM announcement by 18:00' -- targeted searches at 18:00 returned only the $20M reward post; Khaleej Times 18:53 in-window) -- CENTCOM launches Task Force Iron Gate: Iran blockade extended from sea to land borders + Caspian Sea; naval blockade has halted >$25B of Iranian crude exports

totw_analysis: Our read: The blockade just went inland -- CENTCOM's new Iron Gate task force targets Iran's land and Caspian lifelines after $25 billion of oil was stopped at sea. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Choking Iran's war machine -- or strangling ordinary Iranians while the regime adapts through the Caspian?
